tei:div.tei:ab: 7. X. S. Bachs Generalbassbüchlein,A facsimile and English translation of this manuscript was published as J.S. Bach's Precepts and Principles for Playing the Thorough-Bass or Accompanying in Four Parts, Eng. transl. Pamela Poulin (Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1994). Beispiele für „Erleichterung“; Korrektur eines russischen Liedchens.

9. X. Linie zur Chopins
Etude op. 25 Gesdur; neu, Etude Asdur op. 25.
13. X. Korrektur des ersten Teiles der neuen Etude eines neuen Sonatensatzes.Diary October 12: “On Cube’s sonata movement: the exposition improved by corrections.”

16. X. Etude op. 25 No 1, Fingersatz; übergebe ihm Bach-Schemelli-Roth,Herman Roth, ed., 25 Geistliche Lieder (aus dem Schemellischen Gesangbuch) für eine Singstimme und basso continuo (Leipzig: C. F. Peters, [n.d.]), a copy of which, with annotations in Schenker's hand, is preserved at OJ 25/1. entlehnt von Frl. Elias.

19. X. Durchführung im 1. Satz seiner Sonate; Korrektur der Aussetzung zu Roth No 1.Herman Roth, ed., 25 Geistliche Lieder (aus dem Schemellischen Gesangbuch) für eine Singstimme und basso continuo (Leipzig: C. F. Peters, [n.d.]), a copy of which, with annotations in Schenker's hand, is preserved at OJ 25/1: No. 1 is “Auf, auf! die rechte Zeit ist hier,” BWV 440.

27. X. Roth No 2Herman Roth, ed., 25 Geistliche Lieder (aus dem Schemellischen Gesangbuch) für eine Singstimme und basso continuo (Leipzig: C. F. Peters, [n.d.]), a copy of which, with annotations in Schenker's hand, is preserved at OJ 25/1: No. 2 is “Ich steh’ an deiner Krippen hier,” BWV 469. korrigiert.

30. X. Der Vater streikt!There is a long entry in Schenker’s diary for October 30, 1925, which begins: “Cube surprises me with the news of a threat from his father to cease sending him money. We speak on this subject for three-quarters of an hour, and I gain an ever-clearer impression that his father, who is perhaps not in the best financial circumstances at present, is playing a heartlessly cruel game with his son! [...]” Urlinie zur Etude Fmoll op. 25 korrigiert.

3. XI. Roth No 3Herman Roth, ed., 25 Geistliche Lieder (aus dem Schemellischen Gesangbuch) für eine Singstimme und basso continuo (Leipzig: C. F. Peters, [n.d.]), a copy of which, with annotations in Schenker's hand, is preserved at OJ 25/1: No. 3 is “Selig, wer an Jesum denkt,” BWV 498. korrigiert; zur Etude op. 25 No 2: über die verschiedenen Arten des Zugangs zum eröffnenden 6/3-Klang; über das Organische der Diminution in dieser Etude.Diary November 3: “Von Cube pays in shillings.”

9. XI. Roth No 4Herman Roth, ed., 25 Geistliche Lieder (aus dem Schemellischen Gesangbuch) für eine Singstimme und basso continuo (Leipzig: C. F. Peters, [n.d.]), a copy of which, with annotations in Schenker's hand, is preserved at OJ 25/1: No. 4 is “Mein Jesu! was für Seelenweh,” BWV 487. korrigiert.

17. XI. Roth No 5Herman Roth, ed., 25 Geistliche Lieder (aus dem Schemellischen Gesangbuch) für eine Singstimme und basso continuo (Leipzig: C. F. Peters, [n.d.]), a copy of which, with annotations in Schenker's hand, is preserved at OJ 25/1: No. 5 is “Brich entzwei, mein armes Herze,” BWV 444. korrigiert; Mozart Sonate Fdur, 1. Satz bis zur Durchführung – fast aus dem Stegreif gespielt.

20. XI. Brief des Vaters, der angibt, den Sohn nicht
mehr in Wien erhalten zu können!Diary November 20: “Cube shows [me] a letter from his father, who would like to shift the responsibility for security in life, strangely enough, on to me. – I turn down this strong imposition.” Etude op. 10 No 7 neu; zeige die Linie.
24. XI. Mozart Sonate Adur (allenfalls für Fr. Rothberger).Diary November 25: “Cube does not come until 3:30; he has agreed to teach Mrs. Rothberger two hours a week, for 2 dollars.”

27. XI. Etude op. 10 No 7, Fingersatz u. Spiel.Diary November 27: “Cube recounts that Mrs. Rothberger has again cancelled her lesson with him, by telephone. Her excuse: the fee is too high, the children, etc. An unparalleled impudence, intellectual and fiscal niggardliness together!!”

1. XII. Roth No 6Herman Roth, ed., 25 Geistliche Lieder (aus dem Schemellischen Gesangbuch) für eine Singstimme und basso continuo (Leipzig: C. F. Peters, [n.d.]), a copy of which, with annotations in Schenker's hand, is preserved at OJ 25/1: No. 6 is “Kommt wieder aus der finstern Gruft,” BWV 480. korrigiert; Mozart Sonate vorgespielt.
4. XII. Durchführung der eigenen Sonate korrigiert.
11. XII. Rondo – Entwürfe; Etude op. 25 No 1 sehr schön gespielt.

15. XII. Versuch eines eigenen Chorals; Roth No 7 korrigiert.Herman Roth, ed., 25 Geistliche Lieder (aus dem Schemellischen Gesangbuch) für eine Singstimme und basso continuo (Leipzig: C. F. Peters, [n.d.]), a copy of which, with annotations in Schenker's hand, is preserved at OJ 25/1: No. 7 is “Kommt, Seelen, dieser Tag,” BWV 479. — Diary December 14: “Mrs. Pairamall hopes to have gained Baron Popper as a pupil for Cube”.
18. XII. Erster Einblick in die Etude op. 25 No 11, Am, neu.

21. XII. Gärbers Continuo-Satz gezeigt;Probably Heinrich Nikolaus Gerber’s publication of a sonata from Albinoni’s Op. 6 with a continuo realization by J. S. Bach. spielt aus dem Stegreif den letzten Satz der Mozart Sonate Fdur.
29. XII. Gärber, 1. Satz zuende;Probably Heinrich Nikolaus Gerber’s publication of a sonata from Albinoni’s Op. 6 with a continuo realization by J. S. Bach. Mozart-Sonate wiederholt.
5. I. Korrektur seines ganzen Sonatensatzes.
8. I. Scherzo-Pläne.

12. I. Roth No 8Herman Roth, ed., 25 Geistliche Lieder (aus dem Schemellischen Gesangbuch) für eine Singstimme und basso continuo (Leipzig: C. F. Peters, [n.d.]), a copy of which, with annotations in Schenker's hand, is preserved at OJ 25/1: No. 8 is “Jesu, deine Liebeswunden,” BWV 471.: sehr schön ausgeführt, meist dreistimmig. 2. Satz
GärberProbably Heinrich Nikolaus Gerber’s publication of a sonata from Albinoni’s Op. 6 with a continuo realization by J. S. Bach. betrachtet.
15. I. Eine Stelle im Scherzo seiner Sonate; Urlinie zu op. 25 No 2 korrigiert; fragt, ob sich für die Darstellung der Urlinie nicht ein Schema finden ließe?(!)
19. I. Rondo als letzter Satz.
26. I. GärberProbably Heinrich Nikolaus Gerber’s publication of a sonata from Albinoni’s Op. 6 with a continuo realization by J. S. Bach. bis zum Adagio.
29. I. Etude Amoll, Spiel begonnen.
5. II. Rondo – Fortsetzung korrigiert.

9. II. Roth No 9Herman Roth, ed., 25 Geistliche Lieder (aus dem Schemellischen Gesangbuch) für eine Singstimme und basso continuo (Leipzig: C. F. Peters, [n.d.]), a copy of which, with annotations in Schenker's hand, is preserved at OJ 25/1: No. 9 is “Gott, wie gross ist deine Güte,” BWV 462. korrigiert; über den ersten Gedanken der Pathetique. Ueber seinen Wunsch, wegen der unsicheren Verhältnisse, mit der Fugen-Lehre begonnen zu beginnen ; als erste Fuge die 1. Cm-Fuge.Diary February 9: “Cube appears once more to be in a state of disarray, but pays; as a precaution, he embarks on fugue.”

12. II.Diary February 11: “Cube the missed lesson (February 2!) made up, 11 to 12 o'clock.” Zeige ihm die Klischées“Klischée”: literally “printing block,” but often used by Schenker, as here, to mean the printed result, i.e. a music example to be embedded in type. zu Mozarts Gm-Sinfonie.The music examples for the essay on the Mozart symphony in Meisterwerk II.

19. II. Bringt aus Eigenem eine Urlinie zu Chopin Etude op. 10 No 1. February 16: “I advise Cube at least to take up the Chopin Etudes, which have been and always will be the principal staple of [piano] teaching.” – Diary for February 21: “Work on the Scherzo for Brünauer and Etudes 1–3 for Cube.”
23. II. Ueber den Schluss, der keine Durcharbeitung der zeigt; die Cm-Fuge abgeschlossen; – 1. Emoll-Fuge neu.

26. II.
Zur Etude op. 10 No 1: einige Winke.
2. III. Scherzo seiner Sonate zuende korrigiert.

5. III. Chopin op. 10 No 3 Edur; einiges zur Urlinie u. Spiel.There is a long entry in Schenker’s diary for March 5, 1926, which begins: “Cube pays, provisionally but for the last time. Shows [me] the letter from his father, which requests a deferment of payment for the coming months. Cube must now fulfil his father's wish and go to Berlin, to see about gaining some employment!”
9. III. Einiges aus dem Scherzo von Chopin Bm-Desdur gezeigt, namentlich die schraubenartigen Durchgänge.
12. III. Bilder zur Sarabande von Bach gezeigt.
16. III. Appassionata wiederholt u. Chopins Etude Asdur, diese besonders schön.

23. III. Eine neue Bagatelle korrigiert – macht gleichzeitig Shymmis,“shimmy”: a popular American dance of the 1920s. die er der Schwester nach Berlin schickt.Diary March 23: “Cube shows [me] a letter from his sister, which describes the conditions in Berlin as still more unfavorable than those in Vienna. Fulfilling an order from her, he composes shimmies indefatigably.”
26. III. Etude op. 10 No 4, Cismoll: einiges zur Urlinie.

30. III. Etude Fmoll op. 10 No 9; Versuch einer Urlinie, zum Teil richtig, falsch – statt –. Einiges aus dem Buch von Ganche über Chopin.Édouard Ganche, Frédéric Chopin, sa vie et ses oeuvres, 1810–1849 (Paris: Mercure de France, 1913).

6. IV. Versuch, einer Urlinie zu Chopin op. 25 Emoll: Ergebnis – zwar richtig, aber der
Stimmenerweis mangelhaft.Diary April 6: “In front of Cube, clearly expressed, that I see through his father's machinations, that on principle I do not teach without being paid.”

9. IV. Ein Foxtrott!Diary April 9: “Cube, at Vrieslander's request, shows [us] his latest foxtrot.” Ueber Sonaten-Thematik; spiele Haydn Sonaten von Em, Gdur aus Peters I.Probably Louis Köhler’s edition of the Haydn sonatas; the E minor sonata (Hoboken XVI:34) is in volume 1, and Hoboken XVI:40 is the only G major sonata in that volume.]
13. IV. Erste Dmoll-Fuge; allgemeiner Aufriss gelingt d2–a2 sonst nichts!

16. IV. Berçeuse, Urlinie, Form; will sich selbst am Fingersatz versuchen; etwas über die Sonaten von Chopin überhaupt. Ueber Vrieslanders Abneigung gegen die Urlinie u. das Gefühl als entscheidende Instanz.
20. IV. Versuch einer Urlinie zu Chopins Walzer Asdur, op. 34.
23. IV. Fingersatz zur Berçeuse korrigiert.
27. IV. Schlußverstärkung im Scherzo seiner Sonate; – Fingersatz die Berçeuse zuende korrigiert.
30. IV. Vortrag der Berçeuse.
7. V. Chopin Mazurka Am: Linie, Stimmführung.
14. V. Der Vortrag der Etude op. 25 No 2 gelingt restlos, der der Etude op. 25 No 1 weniger gut; wiederholt Brahms-Händel, Thema u. 1.–4. Variation.
28. V. Allgemeines über Pädagogik; schlage die Sonate von Chopin als letztes Stück vor – allgemeiner Umriss.Diary May 28: “Cube remarks that he will send the $120 from Duisburg.”

1. VI. Bringt die Urlinie zur Hmoll-Sonate bis zum 2. Gedanken, dazu Fingersatz, Vortrag, entlehnt mein Heft.Diary June 2: “From Cube (letter sent by a messenger): he was at Stingl's in order that the piano might possibly be made available to me immediately.”

4. VI. Fingersatz bis zur Mitte der Durchführung besprochen; gesteht, drei Tage nur zur Abschrift des 1. Satzes gebracht zu haben! Ich bemerke, daß die Abschrift nicht einmal genau ist! Der Vater ruft ihn telegrafisch ab.Diary June 7, 1926 contains a long entry beginning: “Von Cube comes at 4:30 to say farewell; he says that his father sent a telegram to Munich, promising to send the lesson fees that he owes from Duisburg.” – This is the last lesson in person that Cube had with Schenker. He appears briefly in the lessonbook for 1926/27, but by correspondence.

tei:div.tei:ab: October 7 J. S. Bach’s thoroughbass handbook, examples of “simplification”; corrections to a little Russian song.

October 9 Voice-leading line for Chopin’s
G major Etude from Op. 25; Etude in A major from Op. 25, new.
October 13 Corrections to the first part of the new Etude a new sonata movement.
October 16 Etude Op. 25, No. 1, fingering; I give him Bach–Schemelli–Roth, borrowed from Miss Elias.
October 27 Roth No. 2 corrected.
October 30 His father goes on strike! Urlinie for the F minor Etude from Op. 25 corrected.
November 3 Roth No. 3 corrected. Concerning the Etude Op. 25, No. 2: on the different ways of accessing the opening 6/3 chord; on the organic quality of the diminution in this Etude.
November 9 Roth No. 4 korrigiert.
November 17 Roth No. 5 corrected; Mozart Sonata in F major, first movement, up to the development section – played almost extemporarily.

November 20 Letter from his father which indicates that he can no longer support his son
in Vienna! Etude Op. 10, No. 7, new; I show him the voice-leading line.
November 24 Mozart Sonata in A major (in any event for Mrs. Rothberger).
November 27 Etude Op. 10, No. 7, fingering and playing.
December 1 Roth No. 6 corrected; Mozart Sonata played.
December 4 The development section of his own sonata corrected.
December 11 Rondo – sketches; Etude Op. 25, No. 1, played very beautifully.
December 15 Attempt at a chorale of his own; Roth No. 7 corrected.
December 18 First glimpse of the Etude in A minor, Op. 25, No. 11, new.
December 21 Gerber’s continuo realization shown to him; he plays the last movement of Mozart’s Sonata in F major extemporaneously.
December 29 Gerber, first movement to the end; the Mozart sonata revisited.
January 5 Correction of his entire sonata movement.
January 8 Plans for the Scherzo of his sonata.

January 12 Roth No. 8: very beautifully realized, mainly in three parts. The second movement
of the Gerber studied.
January 15 A passage from the Scherzo of his sonata; the Urlinie for Op. 25, No. 2, corrected; he asks if a formula for the representation of the Urlinie might not be found?(!)
January 19 Rondo the last movement of his sonata.
January 26 Gerber up to the Adagio.
January 29 Etude in A minor, playing begun.
February 5 Rondo – continuation corrected.

February 9 Roth No. 9 corrected; concerning the first subject of the “Pathétique”. Concerning his wish, on account of his uncertain financial circumstances, to begin the study of fugue; to begin with, the first C minor fugue.
February 12 I show him the music examples for Mozart’s Symphony in G minor.
February 19 He brings, on his own initiative, an Urlinie for Chopin’s Etude Op. 10, No. 1.
February 23 Concerning the ending, which does not show any elaboration of the ; the C minor fugue completed; – The first E minor fugue, new.

February 26
A few hints on the Etude Op. 10, No. 1.
March 2 The scherzo of his sonata corrected to the end.
March 5 Chopin Op. 10, No. 3 in E major; some things about the Urlinie and the performance.
March 9 Some things shown in Chopin’s Scherzo in B minor/D major, especially the screw-like passing tones.
March 12 Graphs of Bach’s Sarabande shown.
March 16 The “Appassionata”, revisited, and Chopin’s Etude A major; the latter particularly beautiful.
March 23 A new Bagatelle corrected – at the same time he is writing shimmies, which he is sending to his sister in Berlin.
March 26 Etude Op. 10, No. 4, in C minor: a few things about the Urlinie.
March 30 Etude in F minor, Op. 10, No. 9; an attempt at an Urlinie, to some extent correct but, incorrectly, with – instead of –. Some things from Ganche’s book on Chopin.

April 6 Attempt at an Urlinie for the E minor Etude from Chopin’s Op. 25: the result – is indeed correct, but the
demonstration of the voices is faulty.
April 9 A foxtrot! On thematic design in sonatas; I play him Haydn’s sonatas in E minor and G major from the Peters edition, volume 1.
April 13 First D minor fugue; the general outline is successful, d2–a2; otherwise nothing!

April 16 Berceuse, Urlinie, form; he wants to attempt a fingering himself; something about the sonatas of Chopin in general. On Vrieslander’s aversion to the Urlinie and feeling as the decisive authority.
April 20 Attempt at an Urlinie for the A major waltz in Chopin’s Op. 34.
April 23 Fingering for the Berceuse corrected.
April 27 Strengthening of the ending to the Scherzo of his sonata; – Correction of the fingering of the Berceuse completed.
April 30 Performance of the Berceuse.
May 7 Chopin Mazurka in A minor: voice-leading line, voice-leading.
May 14 The performance of Etude Op. 25 No. 2 succeeds in all respects, that of the Etude Op. 25 No. 1 not as well; Brahms-Handel, theme and first four variations revisited.
May 28 General remarks about pedagogy; I suggest the sonata by Chopin as his last piece – overall outline.
June 1 He brings the Urlinie for the Sonata in B minor as far as the second theme, with fingering and performance; he borrows my volume.

June 4 Fingering as far as the middle of the development section discussed; he admits to having needed three days to make a copy just of the first movement! I remark that the copy is not even precise! His father sends him a telegram.

tei:div.tei:ab: 1. X. Em. Bachs Lehre vom VortragCf. C. P. E. Bach, Essay on the True Art of Playing Keyboard Instruments, Eng. transl. William J. Mitchell (New York: W. W. Norton; London: Cassell, 1949; London: Eulenburg, 1974). gelesen.
3. X. Chopin op. 25, No 1, Urlinie korrigiert.
10. X. Chopin Etude, Fingersatz korrigiert u. Vortrag.
17. X. Vortrag der Etude nach dem Metronom.
19. X. op. 106, zum erstenmal die Fuge gespielt.

22. X. Bachs Vortrag bis §25.Cf. C. P. E. Bach, Essay on the True Art of Playing Keyboard Instruments, Eng. transl. William J. Mitchell (New York: W. W. Norton; London: Cassell, 1949; London: Eulenburg, 1974): §25 is “The Seven-Four Chord,” pp. 286–93.
24. X. Korrektur der Reinschrift der Urlinie von Chopin-Etude.
27. X. Fuge bis Des 3/4.
29. X. Ueber Tempo rubato mit Beispielen.

31. X.. Chopin Etude op. 25, No 11, Amoll, neu; Bild der T. 1–16 korrigiert, Winke für die nächsten Takte.Schenker’s diary for October 31, 1925, records: “I work on the fugue of Op. 106 for Miss Elias.”
3. XI. Letzte Reinschrift der Fuge korrigiert, Grundplan des Ganzen aufgestellt, Grundbrechung des Basses.

5. XI. Bachs Vortrag zuende gelesen.Cf. C. P. E. Bach, Essay on the True Art of Playing Keyboard Instruments, Eng. transl. William J. Mitchell (New York: W. W. Norton; London: Cassell, 1949; London: Eulenburg, 1974).
7. XI. Korrektur der Brahms-Walzer-Reinschrift, No 1 u. 2 (s. vorige Saison).

10. XI. Brahms Walzer No 3 u. 4 korrigiert; bringt die Reinschrift des 2. Satzes von op. 106Elias is here continuing the work of graphing Beethoven’s “Hammerklavier” Sonata, Op. 106 – work that she began in 2024/25: see e.g. Elias’s lesson for October 7, 1924, footnote 1 – in preparation for Schenker’s Eläuterungausgabe of that sonata, which did not reach publication because the autograph manuscript could not be located. u. der Etude op. 25, No 1.

14. XI. Kor-
-rektur der Etude-Reinschrift, 2. Reinschrift verlangt; Korrektur Brahms Walzer No 5.
17. XI. Brahms Walzer No 6 korrigiert.
19. XI. Walzer 7–9No. 7, No. 8, No. 9. korrigiert.Schenker’s diary for November 19, 1925 records: “In the morning I work on Brahms’ waltzes. New checking-through Neue Durchsicht (for Miss Elias).”
21. XI. Etude Am: das erste Bild korrigiert.
24. XI. Fugenbild bis Des 3/4 korrigert.
28. XI. Korrektur der Etude Amoll, das ganze Bild.

1. XII. Ueber einige Lieder (zum Konzert Ivogün);Schenker’s diary for November 28, 1925 records: “Miss Elias brings Paisiello arias that is the theme of Beethoven’s Variations, in addition some volumes of Brahms songs and the score of the Bach cantata that will be heard at the concert given by Ivogün.” – Streichquartett, op. 135, 1. Satz, Linien.
3. XII. op. 135 vierhändig gespielt u. erklärt.
15. XII. Fuge Des 3/4 Bild korrigiert, Fuge vom Anfang gespielt.
17. XII. Brahms WalzerElias has so far studied Nos 1–9 of the sixteen waltzes Op. 39 since the beginning of the saison. korrigiert.
21. XII. Fuge, Anfang des letzten Teiles.

29. XII. Fuge, Engführung, Trillerketten, Bild korrigiert; Oppel gezeigt.In his letter of November 29, 1925, Reinhard Oppel sent Schenker copies of two recent publications: a suite and some etudes for piano solo.
5. I. Fuge bis zur Dominante.
7. I. Brahms Walzer Dm, Gdur, Hm.
12. I. Fuge bis zur letzten Konklusion.
14. I. Brahms Walzer Edur.
16. I. Chopin Etude Em, Bild.

19. I. Fuge bis knapp vor
die Coda, Bild korrigiert.
23. I. Chopin Etude Em, Mittelteil korrigiert.
26. I. Fuge bis fast zum Schluss.
28. I. Brahms Walzer Hdur.
30. I. Etude Em zuende.
4. II. Brahms Walzer Gism korrigiert.
9. II. Fuge abgeschlossen.
16. II. Berçeuse wiederholt.
20. II. Etude, 25 No 9 Gesdur, neu.
23. II. Walzer Asd wiederholt.
25. II. Brahms Walzer abgeschlossen.
27. II. Etude Gesdur Bild korrigiert; erste Winke zum Vortrag.

9. III. Bach Sarabande (Casals Konzert)The works performed in this concert are recorded in Schenker’s diary for March 12, 2026: “Casals: Haydn concerto – Solo-Suite in C major – Schumann concerto.”; Bild recht gut.
13. III. Etuden Asdur, Amoll, Gesdur wiederholt; Etude Desdur neu.
16. III. Letzte Korrektur der Sarabande.

20. III. Cello Sonate Adur (Casals Konzert)Schenker’s diary for March 22, in an extended description, gives: “Casals’s concert (with Schulhof): Beethoven’s Sonata Op. 69 is not performed! […] a Prelude by [Emanuel] Moór […] [Bach’s] unaccompanied Suite in C minor […] two pieces by Schumann, “Langsam” and “Mit Humor” […], a sonata by Bréval.” durchgegangen; zu Strawinsky: Klavier-Konzert; Etude Desdur Urlinie verfehlt, – noch einmal aufgetragen.

23. III. Ueber Casals Spiel der Sonate von Beethoven.Schenker’s comment in his diary for March 22 was: “The players are completely incapable of coming to terms with it, otherwise they would surely have earned a success of the same order as if they were playing the most accessible salon piece by Fauré or Debussy, etc.”

27. III. Etude
Desdur neues Urlinie-Bild u. Fingersatz korrigiert.

30. III. Etwas zu Chopin nach dem Buch von Ganches.Édouard Ganche wrote several books about Chopin, including Frédéric Chopin: sa vie et ses œuvres 1810–1849 (Paris: Mercure de France, 1913), which ran to many editions.
1. IV. Etude op. 25 No 2 Bild korrigiert.

-richt über das Konzert Furtwängler;There is no reference to a Furtwängler concert on or near this date in Schenker’s diary. bemerke einiges zu Beethovens 1. Sinfonie.

16. III. Bringt den Erstdruck der Partita von Seb. BachOf the six partitas for keyboard by Bach (BWV 825–830), Schenker studied the first of these, in B major, most intensively with Elias and Brünauer, in conjunction with the analysis of Beethoven’s Piano Sonata in B, Op. 106. u. Orgel-Fantasien; zeigt den Versuch einer Urlinie der Sarabande.Most probably the Sarabande from the C major Suite for solo cello, which Casals performed at one of his concerts in Vienna and which Schenker assigned to other students (Elias, Brünauer) as an analysis project.
18. III. Synkopen im dreistimmigen Satz; zeigt einen Erstdruck Couperin.

20. III. Ueber die Cello-Sonate Adur (Casals); zu Stravinksys Konzert.Diary March 20: “Hoboken brings Stravinsky's concerto and a few remarks by Fock in the program booklet. I shall keep the concerto at my place for a while.” (Schenker was to use this piece as a counter-example of contrapuntal practice, in the second Meisterwerk Yearbook.)

23. III. Kritik des Casals-Vortrags;Diary March 23: “Hoboken shows me the passages in which he has noted variants or mistakes in Casals's playing; an elegant piece of work.” – Schenker’s diary for March 22 records the concert in an extended description: “Concert: Casals (with Schulhof): Beethoven’s Sonata Op. 69 falls flat! […] a prelude by Moór […] the C major Solo Suite […] two pieces by Schumann “Langsam” and “Mit Humor” […] a sonata by Breval.” Hoboken zeigt seine Notizen, die er während Casals Spiel in sein Stundenbüchlein eingetragen – eine schöne Leistung.

25. III. Fünf-
-te Gattung des zweistimmigen Satzes.
27. III. Menuett Trio: Bild.

30. III. Ueber die Matthäus-Passion (Klenau); Diary March 27 gives a long description of Klenau’s performance of the St. Matthew Passion, which was broadcast on the radio on that date. alla turka begonnen.
1. IV. Fortsetzung der 5. Gattung u. Synkopen im dreistimmigen Satz.
6. IV. Bringt Vrieslander mit.
8. IV. Synkopen dreistimmig.

10. IV. Türkischer Marsch zuende.Diary April 10: “Hoboken appears for his lesson and arrives at 7:30 with Vrieslander for supper. No flowers! The guests stay until 1 a.m., have enjoyed a good meal and good conversation, and ought to have been satisfied.”
13. IV. Bei Rothberger zur Jause.Diary April 13: “3:30 to 5 o'clock at Rothberger's with Vrieslander and Hoboken.”
15. IV. Schubert Walzer,These pieces were published as 36 Originaltänze by Diabelli around 1822. Bilder korrigiert.
17. IV. Versuch Haydn Sonate Gmoll, Entwurf, Fingersatz begonnen.
20. IV. Haydn abgesetzt in Ermanglung einer geeigneten Vorlage; statt dessen Beethoven op. 14 No 2.
29. IV. Aufgaben der Mischungsgattung; Bruckners VII. Sinfonie nachhause genommen, zur Vorbereitung.
5. V. Bruckners VII. Sinfonie, 1. Satz gespielt.Diary May 5: “With Hoboken, Bruckner's Seventh Symphony played four-hands.”
6. V. Mischungsgattung fortgesetzt; Bemerkungen zur Leonoren-Ouvertüre 3.

11. V. Beethoven-Sonate bis
zur Reprise.
22. V. Der 1. Satz beendet.
25. V. Einiges zu Mozart Don Juan; Synthesen Behelfe aus Mendelssohns Schottischer Sinfonie.

27. V. Mozart Sinfonie 1. Satz gezeigt; Fehler in den Partituren; rege die Facsimilerung an.Diary May 27: “I advise Hoboken to save the autograph manuscript of Mozart’s G minor Symphony by having a facsimile edition made. He takes this opportunity to mention an edition of the parts that he obtained a month ago; I ask him to let me see it.” (The symphony in question is identified in the lesson notes for May 29.)

29. V. Bringt neuerworbene Stimmen zur Gmoll-Sinfonie, ältester Druck bei Andrée, ein seltenes Beispiel genauester Wiedergabe der Handschrift; zeigt auch den Erstdruck von Mozarts Hmoll-Adagio u. seines selbständigen Haydn-Andante, das ich aber für unecht erkläre; zeige Stimmführungen in Händels Leçons, Bdur u. in den Variationen; Stimmführungszüge auch in Bachs Emoll-Fuge.Diary May 29: “Hoboken brings the first edition of the parts, published by André, which – a very rare case – show a close agreement with the autograph; in addition, he shows me the first edition of a piano work by Haydn, which I take to be a falsely attributed work, then the Adagio in B minor by Mozart (my first edition is better); finally he shows me a passage from a letter from Vrieslander [...]”
1. VI. Zeige Fehler in Mozarts Sinfonie Fehler in den Partituren.

5. VI. Erklärt sich bereit, auch die Esdur-Sinfonie facsimilieren zu lassen!Diary June 5: “Hoboken declares himself prepared, on his own, also to have the Symphony in E major published in facsimile, and adds that Deutsch is in favor of its publication; [...]”

14. XII. Mazurka Hmoll op. 30 No 2 neu; Mazurka Cisdur op. 50 No 2,The C- minor mazurka from Chopin’s Op. 50 is No. 3, not No. 2. But Schenker marks the work as “new,” and he had already marked Op. 50, No. 3, as a new work at Pairamall’s lesson on October 23, 1925. So he may be referring to a different C minor mazurka, or to the Mazurka in A major, Op. 50, No. 2. neu.

8. III. Bringt Stücke von Rozizky;Ludomir Różycki (1883–1953), Polish composer, who wrote numerous works for solo piano in traditional 19th-century genres (ballades, fantasy pieces, impromptus, intermezzos, nocturnes, and preludes). – Mrs. Pairamall was herself Polish and Schenker was quite liberal in allowing her to play Polish pieces she brought in. Chopin Mazurka Cismoll mit phrygischem d, neu.Chopin wrote five mazurkas in the key of C minor; from Schenker’s reference to “Phrygian d,” the lowered second step of the C minor scale, one can identify this work as Op. 41, No. 1.

15. III. Ueber Ganche, Frl. Dubois usw.;Édouard Ganche (1880–1945) wrote several books about Chopin, including Frédéric Chopin: sa vie et ses œuvres 1810–1849 (Paris: Mercure de France, 1913). Camille Dubois (née O’Meara, 1825–1907) was born in Paris of Irish parents; she studied with Chopin before becoming a concert pianist. The “Miss Dubois” to whom Schenker refers may have been her daughter or granddaughter. bringt „Belege“; über Casals;Schenker’s diary for March 22, in an extended description, gives: “Casals’s concert (with Schulhof): Beethoven’s Sonata Op. 69 is not performed! […] a Prelude by [Emmanuel] Moór […] [Bach’s] unaccompanied Suite in C minor […] two pieces by Schumann, “Langsam” and “Mit Humor” […], a sonata by Bréval.” Chro-
-matische Fantasie wiederholt bis zum Rezitativ.

Brahms Walzer No 4 Emoll: er liest von , ich –.Diary Oct 9: “At 10 o’clock Weisse brings the prints [...] Finally Weisse asks about the Urlinie in Brahms’s Waltz, Op. 39, No. 4 – that he went astray worries him again – I allay these fears as best as I can.” – This lesson note is undated; the above is the only entry before the second lesson (November 2) that relates to the lesson content, so is editorially posited as the lesson date.

2. XI. Chopin Etude Fmoll op 25 No 2 analysiert; über Urlinie-Züge
als Auskomponierung.Schenker’s diary for November 2, 1925, records: “Weisse recounts that, on the occasion of a performance of a Brahms motet, he has once again looked at our studies of the chorale and has now just begun to understand what I meant at the time by Bach’s special art. Once again, he believes that he must defend the concept of Urlinie against the term “Urlinie progressions” (Urlinie-Züge). It becomes ever clearer to me that he is already lumping together the tonal space (Tonraum) in which the Urlinie moves with the Urlinie as understood in composing-out.”
